filename: Projecting Changes in the Drivers of Compound Flooding in Europe Using CMIP6 Models.pdf
title: Projecting Changes in the Drivers of Compound Flooding in Europe Using CMIP6 Models
code_availability: The code to analyze the CMIP6 simulations on Google Cloud, make the projections and reproduce the figures in this manuscript is available at GitHub (https://github.com/Timh37/CMIP6cex) and will be published on Zenodo at a later stage (DOI to be added).
testbed_rationale: The study applies a statistical/empirical multi-linear regression model with EOF reduction to estimate storm surge at European tide gauges and evaluates compound flood driver probabilities. It does not provide a subgrid physics parameterization testbed dataset.
pain_points: Storm surge and river discharge are not direct climate model outputs and require computationally demanding hydrodynamic modeling or offline statistical surrogates.
Enormous data volume (>20 TB daily multi-model CMIP6 output) necessitated cloud-optimized data formats and cloud computing (Pangeo / Google Cloud) to be tractable.
Internal climate variability causes high sampling noise in compound extreme estimates when small ensembles or single initial condition realizations are used.
Sub-daily output is rare across CMIP6, restricting analysis to daily mean and daily accumulated variables, dampening sub-daily peak co-occurrence dynamics.
extraction_notes: The document notes funding by the NSF STC 'Learning the Earth with Artificial intelligence and Physics (LEAP)'. The machine learning component consists of an EOF-based multi-linear regression model trained on ERA5 predictors against GESLA2 non-tidal residuals to emulate storm surge from climate model wind and pressure forcing.
